text: Loaded attn-only-2l on local-full (full precision (local)).
H0 (behavior exists): On the induction dataset, attn-only-2l predicts the repeated token well above chance. Against: baseline accuracy near chance (~1/vocab) or logit diff ~0.
dataset
baseline

Behavior present (local-full): clean mean logprob of answer -2.80, top-1 acc 0.53 (chance ~1/48262, uniform logprob -10.8). Corrupt (first copy replaced) -15.36. Gap ~12.6 nats depends on the first copy.

H1 (where): The clean-vs-corrupt difference is carried by a few layer-1 heads acting at the final position (pos 23), helped by layer-0 heads acting at the first-copy positions (esp. pos 12, the answer token's first occurrence). Against: attribution spread evenly across many heads/positions, or the dominant attribution in layer 0 at the final position only.

H1 (where, re-recorded as open; N0006 was only meant to mark H0/N0002 supported by E0002): The clean-vs-corrupt difference is carried by a few layer-1 heads at the final position (pos 23), helped by layer-0 heads that act at first-copy positions. Against: attribution spread evenly over many heads/positions, or the dominant effect sitting in layer 0 at the final position.
attribution_patching

Attribution screen (local-full, denoise corrupt->clean): head 1.6 dominates (1.47), then 1.7 (0.14); all layer-0 heads <0.04. Layer-1 attn effect sits entirely at final pos 23. Residual attribution peaks at pos 12 (answer's first occurrence) in both layers. Layer-0 role may be underestimated by the linear approximation (it would act via L1 attention patterns, a nonlinear path). Needs exact patching.

H2: Exact activation patching of individual heads (clean into corrupt) recovers most of the clean metric through 1.6 (and some via 1.7), and at least one layer-0 head also restores a substantial share (>20%), which the linear screen missed. Against: no layer-0 head restores >10%, i.e. layer 0 is not specifically needed.
activation_patching

Exact head patching (local-full, denoise, fraction of clean-corrupt gap restored): 1.6 = 0.90, 1.7 = 0.15, every other head |effect| < 0.03 (layer-0 max 0.022 for 0.0). Head 1.6 at final position carries ~90% of the effect.

H2 met its own 'against' condition (no layer-0 head restores >10%, E0004), but the test is confounded. Denoising one L0 head into the corrupt run cannot restore the answer, because in the corrupt run the first-copy tokens (including the answer token at pos 12) are replaced, so any value read from the first copy is wrong anyway. Revised H2': in the CLEAN run, ablating a specific layer-0 head (mean ablation) substantially damages the answer logprob (>30% of the clean-corrupt gap), while the other layer-0 heads do little. Against: no single L0 head ablation costs >10% of the gap.
ablation

Mean ablation in clean run (local-full; clean logprob -2.80, gap to corrupt 12.56 nats): 1.6 -> -12.07 (-9.27, 74% of gap); 0.3 -> -11.65 (-8.84, 70%); 0.0 -> -4.72 (-1.91, 15%); 1.7 -> -3.71 (-0.90, 7%); all other heads |change| <= 0.26. H2' supported: layer-0 head 0.3 is critical, 0.0 secondary.
H2' supported by E0005: ablating 0.3 costs 70% of the gap and 0.0 costs 15%; the other L0 heads cost <2%.

H3 (attention of 0.3): Head 0.3 is a previous-token head. At position p it attends mostly to p-1 (mean attention at offset -1 > 0.5 across positions). Against: its attention at offset -1 is < 0.3, or it peaks at another offset or at BOS.
attention_patterns

Attention (local-full, n=64): head 0.3 puts mean 0.53 on offset -1, consistently ~0.48-0.55 at every query pos >=2. The remainder goes mostly to BOS (~0.32-0.36), with ~0.06 each at offset -2 and self. Next highest offset -1 score is 0.0 at 0.23; all others <=0.13. Head 1.6's most-attended key from the final query is pos 12, the token after the earlier occurrence of the current token. H3 supported.
H3 supported by E0006: 0.3 attends 0.53 to offset -1 (BOS soaks up most of the rest).

H4 (attention of 1.6 and 1.7 at the final query): from query pos 23 (token seq[10]), head 1.6 puts most attention (>0.5) on key pos 12 (seq[11], the token right after the first occurrence of seq[10]), i.e. offset -(seq_len-1) = -11; 1.7 does likewise more weakly. In the corrupt run this attention to pos 12 collapses. Against: 1.6 attention to pos 12 < 0.3 on clean, or similar on corrupt.
attention_patterns

Head 1.6 full pattern (local-full, clean, n=64): from final query 23 it puts 0.64 on key 12 (seq[11] = answer) and 0.25 on BOS. At every second-copy query q (13..23) it attends ~0.47-0.64 to q-11, the token after the earlier occurrence of the current token. In the first copy (q<=12) it parks on BOS (~0.88-0.97). Query 13 is weaker (0.31 on pos 2, 0.58 BOS). Clean side of H4 supported; corrupt side not measured here.

H4 supported (clean side) by E0007: 1.6 attends 0.64 from pos 23 to pos 12 and shows an offset -11 stripe across the whole second copy. 1.7 at the final query has max 0.49 (key not listed as 12; its top key is 0), so 1.7 is weaker/different and stays open.

H5 (composition): 0.3 talks to 1.6 through 1.6's KEY input (K-composition). At key pos 12, 0.3 writes information about the previous token (seq[10]), which 1.6's query at pos 23 (token seq[10]) matches. Test: path patch from 0.3 to 1.6 for each input k / q / v. Prediction: the k path carries a large effect and the q and v paths carry little. Against: the q or v path from 0.3 is as large as k, or the k path is ~0. Caveat: if the tool only denoises, the v-path confound (corrupt first-copy tokens) may suppress every effect; run k first and read the direction.
path_patching

Path patch 0.3 -> 1.6.k (local-full, denoise, dataset corrupt) restores only 0.019 of the gap. Inconclusive by design: in the dataset corrupt run, pos 12 holds a different token, so even perfect attention from 1.6 to pos 12 copies the wrong value. A corruption that keeps the answer token in place is needed.

Build a custom 'previous-token' corruption from the 36 token ids visible in E0001. Make six 12-token sequences: A, B, C (the three dataset examples) and D, E, F (their reversals). Clean = [BOS]+S+S[:11], answer S[11]. Corrupt = same, except first-copy pos 11 (S[10], the token BEFORE the answer's first occurrence) is replaced by an unrelated token. In the corrupt run the answer token still sits at pos 12, but its predecessor no longer matches the current token at pos 23. If induction works via previous-token K-composition, corrupt should fail, and patching clean 0.3 into 1.6.k should restore it. Small n=6 is a limitation.
custom prev-token corruption (retry with metric key 'target')

Custom prev-token corruption (local-full, n=6): clean logprob -3.01 (acc 0.67) vs corrupt -13.37. Replacing ONLY the token before the answer's first occurrence (answer still present at pos 12) destroys the prediction in 5/6 prompts (one stays at -4.16). The model finds the answer by matching its predecessor to the current token.
H5 test with custom prev-token corruption: senders all L0 heads -> 1.6 key
Path patch L0 heads -> 1.6.k (local-full, custom prev-token corruption, n=6, denoise): 0.3 restores 0.77 of the gap, 0.0 restores 0.06, the rest |x|<0.005. K-composition 0.3 -> 1.6 is the main route.

H5b (control): the 0.3 -> 1.6 VALUE path carries little of the effect (<0.15) under the same corruption. Against: v-path effect comparable to k (>0.4). Note: the q path is not tested because this corruption leaves pos 22-23 identical, so the L0 output at the query position is the same in both runs.
H5b control: L0 heads -> 1.6 value

Path patch 0.0/0.3 -> 1.6.v (local-full, same custom corruption): effects 0.0025 and 0.00003. The value path carries nothing here. Caveat: in the corrupt run 1.6 is not attending to pos 12, so this mostly confirms that the effect needs the key to restore attention first.

H5 supported: with a corruption that keeps the answer token, 0.3 -> 1.6.k restores 0.77 (E0010) and 0.3 -> 1.6.v restores ~0 (E0011); prev-token info must be present (E0009). 0.0 contributes a minor 0.06 through k.

H6 (what 1.6 writes): 1.6 writes the answer token directly to the logits. Its direct logit attribution along the answer direction at the final position is the largest of all components (> half of total), and 1.7 is second. Against: 1.6's DLA is small and the effect runs through something indirect (impossible for layer 1 except via the unembed, so a small DLA would mean it suppresses alternatives instead).
H6: logit_diff answer vs another in-context token S[5], custom 6 clean prompts

DLA (local-full, 6 custom prompts, logit diff answer vs in-context token S[5], clean diff 13.75): 1.6 = +11.09 (81%), 1.7 = +1.38, 1.3 = +0.43, all others |x|<0.33. 0.3 direct = -0.19, so its role is purely indirect (via 1.6's keys, E0010). 1.6 boosts the specific answer over other tokens in context. H6 supported.
H6 supported by E0012: 1.6 direct contribution +11.09 of 13.75; 1.7 second at +1.38.

H7 (content, not position): 1.6 finds the key by content match (key pos's previous token == query token), not by a fixed offset of -11. Test: build sequences of length 8 repeated ([BOS]+S8+S8[:7], final query pos 15). Prediction: from pos 15, 1.6's top key is pos 8 (offset -7) with attention >0.4, and the model still predicts the answer. Against: top key at offset -11 (pos 4), or attention to pos 8 < 0.2.
H7: length-8 repeats, query pos 15, expect 1.6 -> pos 8

Length-8 repeats (local-full, n=6): from final query 15, 1.6's top key is pos 8 (0.62), the token after the earlier occurrence of the current token, at offset -7 not -11. The second copy shows the same q-7 stripe (0.37-0.64). In the first copy 1.6 again parks on BOS (>0.9). 0.3 still targets q-1 (top key 14). H7 supported: matching is by content (previous-token key), not a fixed offset.
H7 supported by E0013: 1.6 -> pos 8 (0.62) for length-8 repeats.

H8 (1.7 = weaker second induction head): from query pos 23 on the induction dataset, 1.7 also attends to pos 12 more than to any non-BOS key (attention to pos 12 > 0.15). Against: 1.7's non-BOS attention mass from pos 23 is spread out or peaks elsewhere (e.g. at pos 22/23).
attention_patterns

Head 1.7 (local-full, n=64) from query 23: BOS 0.49; pos 12 0.077 (largest non-BOS key); every other key 0.01-0.03. Across the second copy it shows a faint q-11 stripe (~0.08-0.10). It is a weak, diffuse induction-like head, which matches its small DLA (1.38, E0012) and ablation cost (0.90 nats, E0005).
H8 revised by E0014: 1.7 does peak (among non-BOS keys) at pos 12, but at only 0.077, below the 0.15 threshold. It is a weak, diffuse auxiliary induction head, not a second strong one.

H9 (sufficiency / break test): jointly mean-ablating all 12 heads OUTSIDE {0.0, 0.3, 1.6, 1.7} leaves the clean metric within 1.5 nats of -2.80. Jointly mean-ablating {0.3, 1.6} drops it to near corrupt level (< -11). Against: the complement ablation costs > 3 nats (the hidden helpers matter), or {0.3, 1.6} ablation leaves > -8.
H9a: joint mean ablation of all non-circuit heads
H9b: joint mean ablation of 0.3 + 1.6

Break tests (local-full, n=64, mean ablation): ablating the 12 heads outside {0.0,0.3,1.6,1.7} jointly gives -1.91, BETTER than clean -2.80, so the rest of the model is unnecessary and slightly competes. Ablating {0.3,1.6} jointly gives -12.63 (clean-corrupt gap 12.56, corrupt -15.36, uniform -10.8). H9 supported on both halves.
H9 supported: complement ablation -1.91 (E0015); {0.3,1.6} ablation -12.63 (E0016).

Move to verification on held-out seed 1234 (never used). Circuit = {0.0, 0.3, 1.6, 1.7}, mean ablation. predict(): find the most recent earlier position whose PREVIOUS token equals the current last token (0.3 prev-token key E0006/E0010, content match E0013), and return the token at that position (1.6 copies it to the logits, E0012). Expected weakness: the model is right only ~53% top-1 (E0002), so token agreement with the model will be bounded near that unless predict models its failures, which I have no evidence for.
prev-token head 0.3 -> induction head 1.6 (K-composition), copy next token: not-verified. At least one check failed; the explanation is partial or wrong. See the numbers.

V0001 (local-full, held-out seed 1234, n=200): NOT VERIFIED. (1) Agreement with model 0.605 < 0.9. predict() matches ground truth 1.0, and model accuracy is 0.605, so every disagreement is a model error. In those, the model outputs common tokens ('an', 'i', '\n', 'ing', 'ens') instead of the induction answer. (2) Circuit-ablated: metric -14.68, accuracy 0.00. The check reports fail because fraction_of_clean = -14.68/-3.05 = 4.81 > 0.5; with a negative logprob metric that ratio grows as performance gets worse, so behaviourally this is a clear break. I record the check as failed per the tool and give my reading separately. (3) Circuit alone (others ablated): -2.76, fraction 0.90, accuracy 0.65: PASS. Random same-size ablations: 0.85-1.15 (small change).

H10 (why the model fails ~40%): on the failure prompts, 1.6 still attends to the correct key (pos 12 attention > 0.4), so the failure is in how strongly the copied token beats competing frequent tokens, not in finding the key. Against: on failures 1.6's attention to pos 12 is low (< 0.25), i.e. the matching step itself fails.
H10: 1.6 attention on 5 held-out failure prompts from V0001

On 5 held-out prompts where the model is wrong (from V0001), 1.6's top key from pos 23 is still pos 12, at 0.46 (vs 0.64 on the seed-0 average, E0007), with 0.44 on BOS. The second-copy q-11 stripe is intact (0.40-0.73). H10 supported with nuance: the matching step works on failures but is weaker. The miss happens when the reduced copy signal loses to common tokens ('an', 'ing', '\n'). Which component supplies those competitors was not measured.
H10 supported (E0017): on failures 1.6 still attends 0.46 to pos 12 (> 0.4 threshold), though less than average.

Second verification V0002 using a logit_diff metric (answer vs in-context token S[5]), so that fraction_of_clean is a meaningful ratio (logprob's negative sign broke the 'breaks without circuit' check in V0001). Held-out prompts: 10 NEW sequences built from seed-1234 tokens (5 reversals and 5 cross-splices of the V0001 disagreement prompts; the original failure prompts are excluded so the set is not selected on model failure). Corrupt = the first copy replaced by an unrelated held-out sequence. Same predict() and circuit, default thresholds. I expect agreement still < 0.9 because the model is right only ~60%; that would remain a documented failure.
prev-token 0.3 -> induction 1.6 (logit_diff, held-out spliced/reversed seed-1234 sequences): not-verified. At least one check failed; the explanation is partial or wrong. See the numbers.

V0002 (local-full, 10 held-out spliced/reversed sequences, logit_diff answer vs S[5], clean 11.25): CAUSAL checks PASS. Circuit {0.0,0.3,1.6,1.7} mean-ablated: 1.31 (0.12 of clean, acc 0.0). Everything else ablated: 11.83 (1.05 of clean, acc 0.6). Random 4-head ablations: 0.94-1.07. AGREEMENT FAILS: 0.50 < 0.9. predict() matches ground truth 1.0 and model accuracy is 0.50, so all disagreements are model errors toward common tokens ('.', 'i', '\n', 'ogen', 'an'). Overall status: not-verified (tool). Mechanism is causally confirmed; the model's top-1 errors are not explained.

Stop at 17 experiments + 2 verifications. Raising agreement would require predicting when the induction signal loses to frequent-token competitors. That needs a model of the competitors (likely the direct/bigram path, unmeasured), which a rule-based predict() cannot reproduce without new evidence. Report as PARTIAL: circuit causally verified at full precision, behavioural agreement not.
Report written: benchmarks\induction\report\report.md
